labeler: self (Claude Code Stage 1 inspection of MASTG public corpus)
scope: MASTG Samples — HelloWord-JNI + certificatePinningXamarin. Both have negligible Java-side surface (native or .NET-side core logic). Used as additional boundary cases extending UnCrackable-Level2 / r2pay-v1.0 evidence for limit L1 (Java-only pipeline). No in-scope findings expected.

out_of_scope_known_issues.issue: Core message generation lives in libnative-lib.so via System.loadLibrary("native-lib") + native stringFromJNI(). Java side is a one-line bridge.
out_of_scope_known_issues.note: android:debuggable="true" in manifest is a hardening concern but outside the 6 in-scope categories (crypto/network/permission/intent/hardcoded/reflection_dynamic).

out_of_scope_known_issues.issue: Xamarin app — core pinning logic compiled into App1.dll (.NET CIL inside resources/assemblies/). Java side is mono runtime bindings only, no certificate-validation code in Java/Kotlin.
out_of_scope_known_issues.note: Pinning verification happens entirely on the .NET side, outside scope of jadx + Java-only static analysis.

summary.boundary_evidence: Both APKs add to L1 (Java-only) pipeline boundary count. Neither produced any in-scope finding from Stage 1 analysis. They join UnCrackable-Level2 (libfoo.so anti-tamper) and r2pay-v1.0 (libnative-lib.so token gen) as native-bound / non-Java-bound pipeline boundary cases.
